issue_context.title: Viewport incorrectly calculated in textWysiwyg
issue_context.body:
I have a long text element. 
- In the first instance, the whole text fits the visible canvas area. When I edit everything works as expected.
- In the second instance, I position the text to the right, such that most of it does not fit the canvas. When I click to edit the text jumps to the right.
- In the third instance, I close the sidebar next to the canvas and push the text to the right so that it does not fit the canvas. When I click to edit the text jumps to the right but just a little. 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14358394/138605762-e3be14ac-48b0-41fe-b562-8f95d53d9154.mp4


The size of the jump seems to be correlated with the zoom level:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14358394/138606578-80d096c9-fc25-4dfd-8e29-3d6ac2175182.mp4


It seems to me there is some issue with the sceneCoordsToViewportCoords calculation... but I can't figure out what.
comments: I can't repro the jumping — can you share the scene? Or if it's specific to Obsidian, a repro in CSB (with the offsets)? — That said, can't repro on E+ (which faces other text-related issues such as overflowing bugs).

you can reproduce here: https://ehlz3.csb.app

simply type in any text, make it long, then zoom in such that it does not fit the available screen

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14358394/138658345-5c3786a2-49d1-4f07-a897-8d285cadba7d.mp4

I've played with this... but can't figure out the logic. I clearly don't understand what's going on in the code.

Comparing `viewportCoordsToSceneCoords` to `sceneCoordsToViewportCoords` the math does not seem to work out. I think `sceneCoordsToViewportCoords` should correctly read, though unfortunately, this does not solve the jumping problem.:

```typescript
   const x = (sceneX + scrollX) * zoom.value + zoom.translation.x + offsetLeft; 
   const y = (sceneY + scrollY) * zoom.value + zoom.translation.y + offsetTop; 
```

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/d7cdee37bf621641a1a2df898d1d4a70c0948bc8/src/utils.ts#L223-L264

I am suspecting something is also not right with translateX and translateY, but I can't quite work it out:

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/d7cdee37bf621641a1a2df898d1d4a70c0948bc8/src/element/textWysiwyg.tsx#L19-L36

One more thought on this. Text edit clearly works well when appState.offsetLeft == 0, since normally on excalidraw.com editing text works without the text element jumping around.

Thus I'd double check every line where appState.offsetLeft appears (and offsetTop as well to be thorough).

getTransform (see previous comment) was suspicious to me, because maxWidth seemed off when I was debugging the code.

Having slept on the issue I am now guessing this might be the other error (unfortunately I won't have time to test until late tonight).

I don't think offsetLeft should be effected by zoom at all. offsetLeft is an external factor. Also marginRight  is not divided by zoom.

One more reason to be suspicious of this line, is because the text jumps to the right, but not up or down... i.e. only the horizontal axis is involved in the error... (even though `sceneCoordsToViewportCoords` seems incorrect for both horizontal and vertical axes. 

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/d7cdee37bf621641a1a2df898d1d4a70c0948bc8/src/element/textWysiwyg.tsx#L70-L78
I can't repro this even on the link you've sent. Has it been fixed do you think?
closing this as it was fixed in https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/4630, please reopen if the issue exists

review_comments:
```suggestion
          ((appState.offsetLeft + viewportX) * appState.zoom.value +
```

It shouldn't use `scrollX` because we're in viewport coords, not in scene coords. Same for `updatedElement.x`.

Solves this bug:

![wysiwyg_width](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/139879429-99fdcfd9-6aa9-46c4-ae63-d201bf54fa6d.gif)

But, breaks other things at the same time.

`maxWidth` of the wysiwyg (when zoomed). I've been trying to figure it out and it led me to a rabbit of hole of trying to get rid of the `zoom.translation` thing — I think it's the wrong way to do zooming. We should just update `scrollX/scrollY` when zooming on a cursor.

That I understand. This is why I change the original to `appState.scrollX + updatedElement.x` because `appState.offsetLeft + viewportX` leads to the wrong `maxWidth`.  

What does using `appState.scrollX + updatedElement.x` here break? As apparently that results in the right `maxwidth` value.

> What does using `appState.scrollX + updatedElement.x` here break? As apparently that results in the right `maxwidth` value.

Apparently not — see gif above. I'm surprised it works at all since it's in the wrong coord system (scene vs viewport).

I think the reason it works is it is not positioning the text, merely calculating available width. `(appState.scrollX + updatedElement.x) * appState.zoom.value` will first calculate the viewport width, then convert it to scene width by applying the zoom value.

As I mention it [here](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/4098#issuecomment-951280727): comparing `viewportCoordsToSceneCoords` to `sceneCoordsToViewportCoords` the math does not seem to work out.  The two should transform into each other... but they don't. Since everything else works in Excalidraw, and the sceneCoordsToViewportCoords and vice versa are at play in other places as well... I have a hard time believing that this part of the code is wrong... though I still have my doubts.
